wisdom.name: Wisconsin Diversity Opinion Maps (WISDOM)
wisdom.vintage: Ipsos KnowledgePanel survey, July 2026 (n = 4,775), MRP estimates
wisdom.note: Modeled share of adults who agree. Read from the public map layer; the official data download has not been released yet.

vote.name: 2024 presidential returns by county
vote.org: Compiled by T. McGovern from state reporting
vote.note: Alaska reports by election district, so Alaska boroughs have no value.

chr.name: County Health Rankings analytic data
chr.org: University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute
chr.note: Race-specific values are suppressed where counts are small.

sca.name: Social Capital Atlas
sca.org: Chetty et al. (2022), Opportunity Insights and Meta
sca.note: Uses 2018 county boundaries, so Connecticut planning regions have no value.

wapo.name: Fatal Force database
wapo.note: Fatal police shootings, placed in counties by their coordinates.

vars.label: Discrimination against racial minorities is serious
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults answering yes.
vars.q: Is discrimination against racial/ethnic minority groups a serious problem in the US today?

vars.label: Discrimination against women is serious
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults answering yes.
vars.q: Is discrimination against women a serious problem in the US today?

vars.label: Discrimination against religious minorities is serious
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults answering yes.
vars.q: Is discrimination against religious minorities (for example Jews, Muslims) a serious problem in the US today?

vars.label: Discrimination against people with disabilities is serious
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults answering yes.
vars.q: Is discrimination against people with disabilities a serious problem in the US today?

vars.label: Discrimination against LGBTQ people is serious
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults answering yes.
vars.q: Is discrimination against LGBTQ people a serious problem in the US today?

vars.label: Discrimination against immigrants is serious
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults answering yes.
vars.q: Is discrimination against immigrants a serious problem in the US today?

vars.label: Diversity helps companies succeed
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: Diversity of employee backgrounds – including race, gender, age, and life experiences – helps companies be more successful.

vars.label: White people face as much discrimination
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: White people face as much discrimination as people of color in the U.S. today.

vars.label: Racial disparities are caused by society
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults placing the slider on the societal side of the midpoint.
vars.q: What are racial disparities in education and wealth due to? (slider from individual factors to societal factors)

vars.label: In favor of proven diversity programs
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I am in favor of diversity and inclusion programs that have been shown to be effective in rigorous evaluation studies.

vars.label: Fund research on reducing disparities
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: We should fund more research on the best methods to reduce disparities between groups defined by race, gender, and other demographic characteristics.

vars.label: Diversity training blames White people
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: Many diversity training workshops blame White people or try to make them feel guilty.

vars.label: Protect minorities from discrimination
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I am in favor of policies that protect members of minority groups from discrimination.

vars.label: Affordable housing for racial integration
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: It is important to develop affordable housing options in middle-class neighborhoods to promote racial integration.

vars.label: Schools need not teach history of racism
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: Public schools should not be required to teach the history of racism and discrimination in the U.S.

vars.label: Reduce racial disparities in policing
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I support policies aimed at reducing racial disparities in policing.

vars.label: Reduce racial disparities in health
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I support policies aimed at reducing racial disparities in health outcomes.

vars.label: Equal access to employment
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I support policies that promote equality of access to employment regardless of race, gender, religion, disabilities, and sexual orientation.

vars.label: I create a welcoming environment
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I frequently try to create a welcoming environment for individuals from other racial groups in my community.

vars.label: I would confront a friend who discriminates
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I would confront a friend if they discriminated against someone else.

vars.label: Hesitant to work for a biased company
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I would be hesitant to apply for a job at a company that is known to be biased against a particular social group defined by race, gender, or another demographic characteristic.

vars.label: Uncomfortable interacting with other races
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I feel uncomfortable interacting with people whose race or cultural background is different from my own.

vars.label: Officials should legislate equal access
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: Elected officials should put forth legislation that ensures equal access to personal and professional opportunity.

vars.label: Leaders accountable for inclusion
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: Leaders in organizations should be held accountable for fostering an inclusive workplace culture and achieving measurable diversity goals.

vars.label: Bothered by White people becoming a minority
vars.desc: Estimated share of adults who somewhat agree, agree or strongly agree.
vars.q: I am bothered by the projection that White people will eventually be a numerical minority in the U.S.

vars.label: Trump vote share, 2024
vars.desc: Share of all presidential votes cast for Donald Trump in 2024.

vars.label: Adults with a bachelor's degree
vars.desc: Share of adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher.

vars.label: Median household income
vars.desc: Median household income in the past 12 months.

vars.label: Poverty rate
vars.desc: Share of people below the federal poverty line.

vars.label: Population density
vars.desc: Residents per square mile of land. Analysed on a log scale.

vars.label: Non-Hispanic White residents
vars.desc: Share of residents who are non-Hispanic White.

vars.label: Black residents
vars.desc: Share of residents who are non-Hispanic Black.

vars.label: Hispanic residents
vars.desc: Share of residents who are Hispanic or Latino.

vars.label: Foreign-born residents
vars.desc: Share of residents born outside the United States.

vars.label: Racial and ethnic diversity index
vars.desc: Chance that two residents picked at random belong to different racial or ethnic groups.

vars.label: Racialized economic segregation (ICE)
vars.desc: Index of Concentration at the Extremes: high-income White households minus low-income Black households, over all households. From −1 (deprived) to +1 (privileged). The exposure in Zhang et al. (2023).

vars.label: Income concentration (ICE)
vars.desc: Households earning $100,000 or more minus households under $25,000, over all households.

vars.label: Black/White residential segregation
vars.desc: Dissimilarity index: share of either group that would have to move for an even spread.

vars.label: School segregation
vars.desc: How unevenly students of different races are spread across schools. 0 is even, 1 is fully segregated.

vars.label: Income inequality (Gini)
vars.desc: Gini index of household income. 0 is perfect equality.

vars.label: Black-to-White household income ratio
vars.desc: Median Black household income divided by median White household income.

vars.label: Women's pay per dollar of men's
vars.desc: Women's median earnings for each dollar of men's median earnings.

vars.label: Life expectancy
vars.desc: Average years a person can expect to live.

vars.label: Premature death rate
vars.desc: Age-adjusted deaths before age 75 per 100,000 residents.

vars.label: White–Black life expectancy gap
vars.desc: White life expectancy minus Black life expectancy. The outcome family in Leitner et al. (2016).

vars.label: Black-to-White premature death ratio
vars.desc: Black premature death rate divided by the White rate.

vars.label: Infant mortality
vars.desc: Infant deaths per 1,000 live births.

vars.label: Uninsured under 65
vars.desc: Share of residents under 65 without health insurance.

vars.label: Poor mental health days
vars.desc: Average mentally unhealthy days reported in the past 30.

vars.label: Children in poverty
vars.desc: Share of people under 18 in poverty.

vars.label: Homicide rate
vars.desc: Deaths by homicide per 100,000 residents.

vars.label: Economic connectedness
vars.desc: How many high-income friends low-income residents have, relative to an even mix. The headline measure in Chetty et al. (2022).

vars.label: Exposure to high-income people
vars.desc: Share of high-income people in low-income residents' groups, relative to an even mix.

vars.label: Friending bias
vars.desc: How much less low-income residents befriend the high-income people they are exposed to.

vars.label: Friendship clustering
vars.desc: How often two friends of a person are friends with each other.

vars.label: Support ratio
vars.desc: Share of friendships where the pair has at least one friend in common.

vars.label: Volunteering rate
vars.desc: Share of Facebook users in volunteering or activism groups.

vars.label: Civic organizations
vars.desc: Facebook pages of civic organizations per 1,000 users.

vars.label: Voter turnout
vars.desc: Share of citizens 18 and older who voted in the 2020 presidential election.

vars.label: Upward mobility
vars.desc: Average adult income percentile of children raised by parents at the 25th percentile.

vars.label: White–Black mobility gap
vars.desc: White minus Black adult income percentile for children raised at the 25th percentile.

vars.label: Fatal police shootings
vars.desc: People shot and killed by police per million residents per year, 2015–2024.

vars.label: Black over-representation in police shootings
vars.desc: Black share of people shot and killed by police minus the Black share of residents. Shown where at least 10 deaths have a known race. The outcome family in Hehman et al. (2018).
